title: Luz Stella Rodriguez-Novoa | Senior Social Protection Specialist
gist: A World Bank staff-profile page for Senior Social Protection Specialist Luz Stella Rodriguez-Novoa, whose 2023-2026 post history documents a sustained World Bank push on digitalizing social-registry and cash-transfer delivery systems across Latin America and the Caribbean, with a July 2026 pivot toward homelessness and productive reintegration.

insights.claim: Rodriguez-Novoa's core area of work is 'delivery' — social registers and government-to-persons (G2P) digital payments — with a post history from 2023 to 2026 spanning social registries as a 'gateway to social and economic inclusion,' the digitalization of cash transfers in Ecuador, and labor migration systems in Northern Central America, indicating sustained World Bank investment in digital social-protection infrastructure across Latin America and the Caribbean.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Identifies a multi-year, multi-country World Bank program thread (digital social registries + G2P payments) relevant to govtech and digital-payments vendors targeting LAC public-sector contracts.
insights.locator: Her main areas of interest revolve around innovations in social protection and on the 'delivery' (the 'how to')

insights.claim: Her most recent listed post, from July 2026, is titled 'Reimagining productive lives beyond homelessness,' a new topic area distinct from her prior focus on registries and migration, suggesting an expansion of World Bank LAC social-protection work into homelessness and reintegration.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Flags an emerging World Bank policy focus area (homelessness/reintegration) in LAC social protection worth watching for future program and financing announcements.
insights.locator: Reimagining productive lives beyond homelessness, July 22, 2026

insights.claim: Rodriguez-Novoa works specifically to include migrants and refugees as legitimate recipients of long-term social protection interventions, an explicit institutional priority in her role.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Signals World Bank policy direction toward extending social-safety-net eligibility to displaced populations in Latin America, relevant given regional migration flows.
insights.locator: Luz works to include migrants and refugees as legitimate recipients of long-term social protection interventions.
